title: Optimization of Activated Carbon Nanoparticles for Microwave-Assisted Heavy Oil Recovery: Effects of Salinity and Nanoparticle Concentration
content: This study examines the influence of activated carbon nanoparticle concentration and salinity on microwave heating efficiency for heavy oil extraction. By evaluating varying concentrations of activated carbon in sandstone cores, this research aims to determine the optimal balance that maximizes heating while avoiding pore blockages. Cores were injected with fracturing fluid containing 0.1% to 0.5% activated carbon and subjected to microwave heating. Results revealed that a 0.3% concentration achieved the highest average temperature without significant blockage, while higher concentrations led to blockages, impeding heat transfer. Salinity also played a role, with a 10% sodium chloride solution significantly enhancing heating efficiency, though further increases showed minimal impact. CT imaging confirmed that higher activated carbon concentrations resulted in particle accumulation near the injection side, causing uneven heat distribution. These findings highlight the importance of controlled nanoparticle concentration and salinity for optimizing thermal EOR, with 0.3% activated carbon identified as ideal for balancing heat efficiency and pore permeability. This study suggests that further refinement through advanced imaging like micro-CT scanning could enhance understanding of nanoparticle behavior, supporting more efficient thermal recovery techniques.
